T: Shepherd's pie for four. Set a fifth place for the old man in the chair.
D: In 1977, paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren travel to north London to help a single mother whose council house has turned against her family.
P: Serve the snacks when Janet and Margaret play with their homemade spirit board under the bedcovers.
S: Peggy Hodgson's sausage rolls with brown sauce
Peggy keeping four kids fed on a single mum's money in Enfield

Flaky puff pastry rolls of pork sausage, onion and sage, brushed with egg and baked golden, with brown sauce. Heat the oven to 200C. Mix 500g pork sausage mince with 1 finely chopped brown onion, 1 tsp dried sage and 1/2 tsp white pepper. Cut 2 thawed sheets of puff pastry in half, lay a log of filling along each strip, roll up and press the seam closed. Cut each roll into 4, set seam side down on a lined tray and brush with beaten egg. Bake for 25 minutes until puffed and deep golden, cool for 5 minutes and serve warm with brown sauce.
Bill Wilkins's armchair cheese and pickle toasties
the old armchair in the corner of the front room that nobody wants to sit in

Buttered white bread fried golden around vintage cheddar, brown pickle and a smear of hot mustard. Butter one side of 8 slices of white bread with 40g soft butter. Turn 4 slices butter side down, spread thinly with 2 tsp hot English mustard, pile on 200g grated vintage cheddar and 4 tbsp brown pickle, then close with the other slices, butter side up. Fry two at a time in a frying pan over medium low heat, pressing with a spatula, for 4 minutes a side until golden and the cheese has melted. Cut into triangles and serve hot.
M: a hot dinner on the table at 284 Green Street before the lights go out

Lamb mince braised with carrot, celery and thyme, peas through it, under buttery mash with a cheddar crust. Cook 1 diced brown onion, 2 diced carrots and 2 diced celery sticks in 1 tbsp oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft. Turn up the heat, add 800g lamb mince and brown it well. Stir in 2 tbsp tomato paste and 2 tbsp plain flour, then 500ml beef stock, 1 tbsp worcestershire sauce and 1 tsp dried thyme, and simmer for 30 minutes until thick. Meanwhile boil 1.2kg floury potatoes until tender and mash with 60g butter and 100ml milk, then season. Stir 150g frozen peas through the mince, season and tip into a 2 litre baking dish. Spread the mash on top, rough it up with a fork, scatter with 60g grated cheddar and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
W: Janet's school jam roly-poly with custard
Janet back at school with the whole street talking

Soft butter pudding dough rolled around raspberry jam and steam-baked, sliced thick under hot vanilla custard. Heat the oven to 180C. Rub 125g grated cold butter into 250g self-raising flour, 2 tbsp caster sugar and a pinch of salt, then stir in 150ml milk to make a soft dough. Roll out to 30cm by 20cm, spread with 150g raspberry jam leaving a 2cm border, roll up from a short side and pinch the ends. Wrap loosely in buttered baking paper and foil, sit on a rack over a roasting tin half full of boiling water and bake for 40 minutes. Meanwhile heat 500ml milk. Whisk 4 egg yolks, 60g caster sugar and 1 tbsp cornflour, pour on the hot milk, return to the pan and stir over low heat until thick, then add 1 tsp vanilla. Rest the pudding for 5 minutes, slice thickly and serve with the custard.
K: sitting up through the night with the tape recorder running

Whisky with honey and lemon topped with boiling water, a clove-studded lemon slice and cinnamon. Press 2 cloves into each of 4 lemon slices. Divide 3 tbsp honey, the juice of half a lemon and 160ml whisky between 4 heatproof glasses. Top each with 150ml boiling water and stir, then add a lemon slice and a piece of cinnamon stick and leave for a few minutes. Serve hot.

dishes.make_ahead: Assemble the toasties up to 4 hours ahead, wrap and chill; fry just before serving

steps.text: Butter one side of each slice of bread.
Turn 4 slices butter side down, spread thinly with mustard, pile on the cheddar and pickle and close with the other slices, butter side up.
Fry in a frying pan over medium low heat, pressing with a spatula, for 4 minutes a side until golden and melted. Do it in two batches.
Cut into triangles and serve hot.

dishes.make_ahead: Make the pie to the cheddar stage up to 2 days ahead and chill, or freeze for 1 month; bake from cold for 40 minutes

steps.text: Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the oil in a large pan over medium heat until soft.
Turn up the heat, add the lamb mince and brown it well, breaking it up.
Stir in the tomato paste and flour, then the stock, worcestershire and thyme. Simmer gently, stirring now and then, until thick.
Meanwhile boil the potatoes until tender, drain and mash with the butter and milk. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir the peas through the mince, season and tip into a 2 litre baking dish. Heat the oven to 200C.
Spread the mash over the top, rough it up with a fork and scatter with the cheddar.
Bake until the top is golden and the edges bubble.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

veg.make_ahead: Make the pie to the cheddar stage up to 2 days ahead and chill, or freeze for 1 month; bake from cold for 40 minutes

steps.text: Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the oil in a large pan over medium heat until soft.
Turn up the heat, add the mushrooms and cook until dark and dry, then stir in the lentils.
Stir in the tomato paste and flour, then the stock, soy sauce and thyme. Simmer gently, stirring now and then, until thick.
Meanwhile boil the potatoes until tender, drain and mash with the butter and milk. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir the peas through the lentils, season and tip into a 2 litre baking dish. Heat the oven to 200C.
Spread the mash over the top, rough it up with a fork and scatter with the cheddar.
Bake until the top is golden and the edges bubble.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

dishes.n: Janet's school jam roly-poly with custard
dishes.make_ahead: Make the custard up to 2 days ahead and reheat gently; roll and wrap the pudding up to 4 hours ahead and chill, then bake

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180C. Rub the butter into the flour, sugar and salt, then stir in the milk for the dough to make a soft dough.
Roll out on a floured bench to 30cm by 20cm, spread with the jam leaving a 2cm border, roll up from a short side and pinch the ends closed.
Wrap loosely in buttered baking paper, then foil, and sit it on a rack over a roasting tin half full of boiling water.
Bake until risen and firm.
Meanwhile heat the milk for the custard. Whisk the yolks, custard sugar and cornflour, pour on the hot milk, return to the pan and stir over low heat until thick, then add the vanilla.
Rest the pudding for 5 minutes, slice thickly and serve with the hot custard.

Divide the honey, lemon juice and whisky between 4 heatproof glasses.

Serve hot.

Press 2 cloves into each lemon slice.
Divide the honey and lemon juice between 4 heatproof glasses.
Pour in the hot ginger tea, stir, add a lemon slice and a piece of cinnamon stick to each and steep for a few minutes.
Serve hot.
